df=collections.Counter()
for *_, allset in arts: df.update(allset)
N=len(arts); idf={w: math.log((N+1)/(c+1))+1 for w,c in df.items()}
items=[]
with open('market.csv', newline='') as f:

        qt=set(toks((r.get('title') or '')+' '+(r.get('background') or '')))

            score=sum(idf.get(w,1) for w in inter)+4*sum(idf.get(w,1) for w in tinter)

        if best:
            items.append((best[0],r['qid'],r['resolution_date'],r['title'],r['my_prediction'],best))
for score,qid,rd,title,my,best in sorted(items, reverse=True)[:80]:
    s,at,src,date,rare,tinter,n=best
    print(f'{score:.1f} Q{qid} {rd} | {title}')
    print('  my',my)
    print(f'  art {date} {src} | {at}')
    print('  title_terms',tinter,'rare',rare,'n',n)

The 19-year-old set the fastest time of one minute 28.778 seconds on his first attempt in the final shootout phase of qualifying. For Antonelli, playing it safe paid off. It was the 50th pole for an Italian driver. He heads into the weekend fired up from having secued his first pole and victory two weeks ago in China as he bids for a first win at Suzuka, an old-school layout renowned as one of the great drivers' tracks.
